clues.title: Landscape: flat desert
text: The UAE typically features a flat **desert landscape**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Flat, sandy desert terrain.

clues.title: Road lines: yellow edges
text: Outer roadlines are **yellow**, middle lines either **white **or **yellow**.
NOTE: Other Middle Eastern countries, like Jordan, Israel and Oman, also use these lines.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Yellow lines on the outside, and the middle line is white or yellow. Jordan, Israel and Oman use these too, so check other clues.

clues.title: Google car: white with black roof rack
text: In almost all Generation 3 coverage, a **white car** with visible black roof racks was used.
NOTE: The UAE is the only Middle Eastern country where a white Google car can be found.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In almost all older Gen 3 coverage (blurrier, softer colours), a white car with a visible black roof rack. It is the only white Google car in the Middle East.

clues.title: Google car: white pickup, often blurred
text: In Generation 4 coverage, a white **pickup truck** with a trekker camera was used for much of the coverage. In a lot of the coverage, the truck is completely [blurred out](https://maps.app.goo.gl/gz9p2N59bhqFxtvT7).

NOTE: A similar truck can be found in [Qatar](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9vAjK8jA8Upvm1pq8) and [Oman](https://maps.app.goo.gl/CAfekUi6QZ6TF6bV7). In the UAE the antenna at the front of the cabin is on the middle of the car, while in Qatar it is on the left.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Newer Gen 4 coverage often uses a white pickup truck with a trekker camera, frequently blurred out. The front-cabin antenna sits in the middle here, but on the left in Qatar. Oman has a similar truck.

differs.how: Antenna at the front of the cabin is on the left, not the middle

clues.title: Google car: black car, brake light visible
text: You can also find regular Generation 4 coverage taken with a **black **car. The brake light is commonly visible.
NOTE: A similar Generation 4 black car can be found in [Israel](https://maps.app.goo.gl/8AR2EPX61mXVjE1M6).

images.caption: Road markings seen from the car, with Front and Back labels for the two views

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Some newer Gen 4 coverage uses a black car, and you can often see its brake light. Israel has a similar black Gen 4 car.

clues.title: Language: Arabic with English alongside
text: The official language in the UAE is Arabic. Its script can be identified by its **lines and dots**.
NOTE: Due to high tourism, signs in the UAE often have English writing alongside Arabic. While this is also common in Qatar and Oman, it is not common in Jordan.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Arabic script (lines and dots), and signs often carry English too because of heavy tourism. Qatar and Oman are similar, but English is uncommon on signs in Jordan.

differs.how: English is not common on Jordanian signs

clues.title: Houses: light stone, reddish sidewalks
text: Houses in residential areas are typically made of **light-coloured stone**. Reddish stones are often used for sidewalks.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Houses in residential areas are typically light-coloured stone, and reddish stones are often used for the sidewalks.

clues.title: Sign: black-and-white striped signposts
text: Many signposts in the UAE have **black-and-white stripes**.
NOTE: Within the Middle East, striped signposts are also found in Oman.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Many signposts have black-and-white stripes. In the Middle East, only Oman has these as well.

clues.title: Curbs: striped black-white or black-yellow
text: Similarly, almost all curbs are **striped**. They can be either black-and-white, or black-and-yellow.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Almost all curbs are painted with stripes, either black and white or black and yellow.

clues.title: Roads: many divided roads and roundabouts
text: **Divided roads** and **roundabouts** are both very commonly seen in the UAE.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Divided roads and roundabouts are both very common.

clues.title: Pole: dark brown wood, three insulators on bar
text: Electricity poles in the UAE are mostly made of **dark brown wood**. The pole tops consist of **three insulators**, symmetrically attached to a **horizontal metal bar**.
NOTE: Similar poletops can be found in Oman. Jordanian poletops may look similar, but they are usually made of grey concrete, and the insulators are more spaced out.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Dark brown wooden poles with three insulators placed symmetrically along a horizontal metal bar. Oman has similar tops.

differs.how: Grey concrete poles with more widely spaced insulators

clues.title: Roads: unpaved residential streets
text: Although the UAE is a wealthy country, it is not uncommon for residential roads to be **unpaved**.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Even though it is a rich country, residential roads are often unpaved.

clues.title: Glitch: torn picture (rifts)
text: **Rifts** can occasionally be found in the UAE.
NOTE: They are most commonly found in Albania, Montenegro and Senegal.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Occasionally you may see rifts, glitches where the picture looks torn. They are much more common in Albania, Montenegro and Senegal.

differs.how: Rifts are far more common there
Rifts are far more common there
Rifts are far more common there

clues.title: Coverage: mostly northeast corner only
text: Coverage in the UAE is mostly limited to the **Northeastern part** of the country.
NOTE: The only car coverage outside of this region exists on Sir Baniyas Island. All other remote coverage was taken by a trekker.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Car coverage is mostly limited to the northeastern part of the country. The only car coverage elsewhere is on one island. All other remote coverage is trekker.

clues.title: Skyline: many skyscrapers, a tall iconic tower
text: The skyline of Dubai is dominated by numerous **skyscrapers**, including the iconic Burj Khalifa.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A skyline packed with skyscrapers, including the famous Burj Khalifa.

clues.title: Landscape: mountains only in the far east
text: **Mountains** are only found in the far east of the country.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Mountains appear only in the far east of the country.

clues.title: Landscape: light-coloured mountains to the east
text: You can easily recognise the Northern part of the emirate of Ras al Khaimah thanks to the **light-coloured mountains** visible to the east.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the north, light-coloured mountains visible to the east point to the emirate of Ras al Khaimah.

clues.title: Landscape: mountains west, flat land east
text: If you see **mountains to the west**, and flatness to the east, you are likely near the Gulf of Oman, in the extreme East of the country.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: If mountains are to the west and the land is flat to the east, you are probably near the Gulf of Oman in the extreme east. Oman looks similar.

clues.title: Google car: white, side mirrors, sparse plants
text: This rare white Google car with visible side mirrors and sparse vegetation is found on **Sir Baniyas** Island.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A rare white Google car with visible side mirrors and sparse vegetation, found on one island.

clues.title: Google car: sidewalk trekker
text: In some parts of Dubai, including the [old town](https://goo.gl/maps/CXsP5xq4fAtX7Ds47), a Generation 4 **sidewalk trekker** was used. Sometimes, the employee’s black hair is visible.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In parts of the biggest city, including the old town, a Gen 4 trekker was carried on the sidewalk. You can sometimes see the operator's black hair.

clues.title: Sign: blue street names, narrow metal border
text: These **blue** street name signs, with a narrow **metal border**, are specific to Dubai.

images.caption: A blue street name sign in Arabic and English with a narrow metal border

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Blue street name signs with a thin metal border, specific to the biggest city.

clues.title: Coverage: trekkers at two forts and a zoo
text: The city of **Al Ain** has several trekkers, far away from the area with car coverage: two forts ([Qasr Al Muwaiji](https://goo.gl/maps/nbGPsLFqTb1terfh9) and [Al Jahili](https://goo.gl/maps/xMzzvnsvnPqw5ywR9)) and a [zoo](https://goo.gl/maps/XAVgfZVCEW1VPkUE9).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: In the inland city of Al Ain, trekker coverage far from the car coverage covers two forts and a zoo.

clues.title: Coverage: racetrack, east of capital
text: This **racetrack** coverage is found slightly east of Abu Dhabi.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Racetrack coverage slightly east of Abu Dhabi.

clues.title: Coverage: trekker amid sand dunes
text: Remote trekkers, with **sand dunes** all around, can be found in the far south of the country, between the towns of Taraq and Alyhyali.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Remote trekker coverage surrounded by sand dunes in the far south, between the towns of Taraq and Alyhyali.

clues.title: Google car: silver Gen 3 car
text: If you have vibes/other clues that you are in the middle east and you have silver car in Gen3 that means you can only be in UAE.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: If it feels like the Middle East and you see a silver Gen 3 car (older, blurrier camera), you can only be in the UAE.
